metadata.description: Standards bypass configuration for this branch

bypass.reason: Wire-identity primitives (_stdout_target, _session_dir_of, _cmdline, _looks_like_ours). Their one public caller, arm_wire, registers a live wire, installs a SIGTERM handler, and sweeps and signals other live wires by pid, so a test through it acts on real processes. Each row pins one primitive's answer for one platform, with the platform pretended on wire's own sys name and ps/lsof stubbed. 152 is the host probe that decides whether this machine can see fd/1 (fleet green, 2026-10-04).

Pins a cache guarantee no public answer shows: an unchanged transcript is parsed once, then every tick reuses the verdict. The counter wraps the real _tail_lines and returns its answer, so the verdicts asserted are the product's.

File-wide because the stdlib_patch checker passes no line; the one patch it covers is _case_insensitive_glob. Every other stdlib name in this file is swapped on the module under test only (pretend_platform). It emulates a case-insensitive (Windows) directory listing so the exact-case *_REGISTRY.json filter can be shown load-bearing from Linux, where the effect cannot occur on disk. The wrapper widens the real glob and monkeypatch restores it; a product seam per glob would be a door for tests alone. Same reason as memory's case-fold fixtures (leg 11).

An identity pin, not a reach: seat_email's owner lookup must BE guard.owner_address, one implementation of 'who owns this project' (the 2026-08-21 two-answers bug). No behaviour shows the difference until a second copy drifts.

The default store location is the contract (next to the code that owns it, from any cwd). Its public routes, register() and wake_in() with no store named, write the live .watchdog/ of the seat running the suite, which the conftest seal exists to prevent (2026-09-27, a test armed a real wire). The test carries live_default_store and only resolves the path.

CLI handler contract (fleet green, devpulse 2026-10-04; ai_mail leg 9 precedent). A _handle_* return is 'command recognised', not 'it worked': the router stops on True. Every line follows a cli error(), which marks the command failed and sets the non-zero exit, so the caller is told by that flag, never by the bool.
CLI handler contract, as compass.py: each True follows a cli error(), which marks the command failed and sets the exit.

Router contract: a module that raised is reported through cli error() (exit non-zero, 'A defect in the module, not an unknown command'); True stops the router from answering 'Unknown command' on top of it.

Fail closed. 91: a key file that exists but is not hex reads as no key, so nothing is signed or verified (logged as an error). 195: an unreadable caller passport answers '', which matches no seat, so the ceremony refuses. Neither can grant anything.

owner_address answers None for 'no owner resolved' by contract (docstring): its callers are refusal-message builders, which word it as 'no owner is sealed or readable', and the watchdog dispatch register, which raises RegisterUnavailable on it. The access decision does not read it: _owner_decision refuses an unreadable registry on its own (2026-10-04).

An unreadable CHANGELOG gives no headline, and compose_body then says so in the mail itself ('could not be read on the sending machine - open the release notes above'); the failure is logged as an error. The reader is told, not misled.

None is 'cannot read this passport', and its one caller (discover_managers) lists that path in skipped with reason 'passport unreadable - see the log', which the run reports. Never counted as a non-manager.

200/208: liveness fails safe to alive (a check that cannot run never declares a running agent dead; the lock and timeout still end the watch). 205: ProcessLookupError is the answer 'dead', not a failure. 211: any other os.kill error is an invalid pid, dead. 243: an unreadable transcript tail feeds only the advisory stall signal, never the exit verdict. 447: FileNotFoundError between exists() and read is a lock released in that instant, absent. The unreadable lock itself answers {} (held), 2026-10-04.

Liveness, as agent.py: an unreadable /proc status is not proof of a zombie (174), a Windows check that cannot run answers alive (256), ProcessLookupError is the answer dead (261), PermissionError means the process exists (265). A wrong 'alive' costs a slower reap; a wrong 'dead' would drop a live watch.

None is the documented 'stdout target unknown', the same answer /proc gives for an unreadable fd/1 (_stdout_target docstring); the wrapper is then classified as having no session, never as a wrong one.

compass/ is the devpulse-owned Compass decision store (SQLite/FTS5 — db + wal + shm) which needs its own directory. Legitimate data subdir, not operator-config (custom_config/) nor auto-gen root data. Sanctioned exception per #643.

Watchdog presentation layer — console.print() IS the output. Same sanctioned shape as the feedback display handlers below: every function here renders a handler result dict for the operator and decides nothing. Split out of apps/modules/watchdog.py on 2026-08-22, which had reached 692 lines across r2/r3/r4 and broke the 600-line module ceiling; the display functions were the cohesive third that shared no state with the routing code.
Feedback handler — console.print() IS the output. Display functions are the handler's purpose.

_FileLock uses Python _PrivateClass convention (underscore prefix + PascalCase).
_AIPASS_ROOT fallback for ai_mail inbox resolution. Known gap — needs registry-based path resolution.
format_wait() has 5 passing tests. Public utility for schedule display, not called in production yet.
